ui_bugs.issue: ESLint pragma `// eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` on line 75 referred to a rule from `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` which is NOT installed in this project — CRA/webpack-dev-server treated it as a compile-time ERROR ('Definition for rule react-hooks/exhaustive-deps was not found') and rendered a full-viewport overlay iframe (#webpack-dev-server-client-overlay) intercepting all pointer events, blocking every click on admin routes. Removed the pragma to unblock testing. Runtime behavior unchanged (useCallback deps list already correct).

action_items: OPTIONAL: If the team wants to keep the exhaustive-deps pragma (for future reinstatement of eslint-plugin-react-hooks), either install that plugin OR configure the shared CRA/ESLint config to register the react-hooks/* rules. Until then any pragma referencing a non-existent rule triggers a CRA compile ERROR and blocks the whole app behind the webpack overlay — see AdminFirstPayoutQueue.js:75 fix.
OPTIONAL: Consider adding a repo-wide grep guard in CI: `grep -rn 'eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks' src/` to catch this class of latent CRA compile errors before merge.

OPTIONAL: /api/bank-transfer/admin/first-payout-queue does not currently take `?threshold=` override — admin can only change threshold via app_settings. Fine as-is, but a query-param override would enable a preview-what-if slider without persisting.
critical_code_review_comments: manual_bank_transfer.py L1352-1391 (threshold GET/POST): the value bound is `0 <= val <= 5000` — good guard. But POST accepts raw dict payload (`payload: dict`) instead of a Pydantic model — recommend `class ThresholdRequest(BaseModel): value: Optional[float]` for validation + OpenAPI docs. Currently `{value: 'abc'}` returns 400 correctly via ValueError catch, but silent-key payloads (`{val: 500}`) get treated as null-clear.

manual_bank_transfer.py L1414: aggregation matches status ∈ [paid, completed, success] but /admin/first-payout-threshold sample logic only mentions 'paid'. Confirm 'completed'/'success' are truly reachable states elsewhere in the codebase before relying on them, else prune to avoid confusion.
AdminFirstPayoutQueue.js L75 (fixed by test agent): as noted, unknown-rule pragma is a CRA compile error. This is a repeat class of bug — worth adding a linter step to CI to catch.

manual_bank_transfer.py L1442 `days = int((now - dt).total_seconds() // 86400)` — floors the delta. A request created 3.9 days ago returns days_waiting=3 → is_urgent=false. If policy is 'urgent after 3 full days' this is correct; if 'urgent after 72h' consider using > 3 * 86400 seconds directly or `math.ceil` for user-friendly rounding.

manual_bank_transfer.py L1394-1482 queue endpoint has NO auth dependency (no `Depends(get_current_admin)` or similar). If this route is meant to be admin-only, the endpoint currently allows anyone with backend URL to enumerate pending withdrawal requests + full bank details (a/c number, IFSC). HIGH PRIORITY: verify auth is enforced at gateway/middleware level, OR add explicit admin-guard.

rca of the issue: Root cause of previous iteration's seeding failure (E11000 dup key) was confirmed FIXED via partialFilterExpression on users.email index — verified by seeding multiple test users with random UUID-based emails and observing zero dup-key errors in Mongo. Root cause of prior FE admin_uid/admin_id mismatch was fixed and verified via a live POST /admin/mark-paid with {admin_id: 'admin-test-123'} → 200 + persisted state has processed_by='admin-test-123'. NEW issue found this iteration: an ESLint pragma in AdminFirstPayoutQueue.js referenced a rule from a plugin that isn't installed in the project (eslint-plugin-react-hooks). CRA treats unknown-rule pragmas as compile errors, and the webpack-dev-server injects a full-viewport iframe overlay for compile errors, which intercepted every pointer-event and made the app effectively unusable in the preview environment. Mitigation: removed the pragma (line 75 was a no-op anyway since the deps list `[user?.token]` matches the useCallback body). Long-term fix: either install the react-hooks plugin OR add a lint pre-commit hook to catch dangling pragmas.
